body.statement: If \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\) and \(d\le4\gamma\), then constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\), satisfy \(c r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\le\rho_n^*\le C r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). In particular, \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=1/10\), and \(\beta=9/10\) yield \(\rho_n^*\asymp n^{-2/5}\).
body.justification: The asymmetric example proves that a first-order nuisance product condition is not the operative no-penalty mechanism.
body.gap: Hahn1998 proves propensity ancillarity for regular ATE efficiency; no prior result gives this nonregular testing equality region.
body.consumer: The theorem identifies a broad regime where an observational implementation pays no rate cost relative to receiving the true assignment law.
